# `.claude/` — the beads workflow for Claude Code

**These files are generated by [beads-pm-kit](../.beads/PRIME.md).** Edit the kit and re-run
`bd-kit install --into .`; a hand-edited copy is detected by `bd-kit diff` and refuses the next
update. Each file carries a stamp line naming the kit version and the hash it was built from.

## The commands

| Invoke | Use it when | Writes to the board? |
|---|---|---|
| `/bead-split <file.md \| dir> [--apply]` | a spec, plan or roadmap in markdown needs to become an epic plus sized children | only with `--apply` |
| `/bead-estimate <id> \| --epic <id> \| --backfill [--apply]` | a bead has no size, or a whole board needs backfilling | single id yes; batch modes only with `--apply` |
| `/bead-take <bead-id>` | take exactly one bead, work it in a worktree, close it with evidence | yes |
| `/bead-loop [--include-partial]` | each round picks exactly ONE workable bead and delivers it | yes |
| `/bead-fleet [--batch N]` | several independent `auto-ok` beads, in parallel, one worktree each | yes |
| `/bead-pm-loop [--fleet N] [--report-every N]` | run the board with WIP limits, gates, calibration and reporting cadence | yes |
| `/bead-report [epic-id]` | board status, completion rate, flow health, risks | no |
| `/bead-forecast [--epic <id>] [--apply]` | when the work will finish, with honest bands | only with `--apply`, and only metadata plus a note |
| `/bead-audit [epic-id \| label \| ids…]` | you suspect "already done" is not true | yes, main loop only |

The usual order: `/bead-split` → `/bead-estimate --backfill` → `/bead-pm-loop` → `/bead-report`.

## The two contracts every command relies on

**Classification.** Exactly one of `auto-ok` / `auto-partial` / `needs-human` on every non-epic
bead, with the measurable reason in that bead's notes. `bead-loop` §0 is the single source of
truth; the other commands point at it and never copy it. These labels are this project's
swimlanes, so an unclassified bead is a visible red lane, not private bookkeeping.

**Size.** Exactly one `size:*` label on every active non-epic bead, mirrored into
`estimated_minutes`. Epics are never sized. `size:XL` is not claimable. `bead-estimate` §0 is
the source of truth, and the same text reaches every session through `.beads/PRIME.md`.

## Where the numbers come from

`bead-report` and `bead-forecast` both call `.beads/pm/board.py`, installed by the kit, so they
cannot disagree about what a point or a percentage means. It can be run directly:

```bash
python3 .beads/pm/board.py report
python3 .beads/pm/board.py forecast --epic <id>
python3 .beads/pm/board.py report --json
```

It refuses to print a delivery date when the sized history cannot support one. That refusal is
a feature: a confident wrong date is the most expensive thing a report can emit.

## The full loop, written out

`.beads/pm/guide.md` walks the nine commands as one cycle: spec to board, board to sized work,
work to report, report to forecast, forecast to audit, and back. Also in
`.beads/pm/guide.vi.md` (Tiếng Việt) and `.beads/pm/guide.zh-cn.md` (简体中文).

## Anti-patterns measured on `bd 1.2.2`

All of these run, exit 0, and give the wrong answer — which is why they are written down
rather than remembered.

- `bd create --file <md>` ignores `--labels`, `--parent` and `-p` **without saying so**: the
  beads come out P2, unlabelled and unparented. Its markdown batch format carries no per-issue
  metadata either, and `--dry-run` errors out when combined with `--file`. `bead-split` uses
  `bd create --graph` for exactly this reason.
- `bd ready --label-any` **does not filter** — it returns beads without the requested label,
  `needs-human` ones included. The AND form `--label <x>` works. Filter labels in Python.
- `bd search` excludes closed beads by default, so a dedupe without `--status all` recreates
  the bead you just closed.
- `bd list --json` has **no `is_blocked` field** and leaves blocked beads at status `open`.
  Measured on a 75-bead board: five beads were blocked and a report built on `bd list` alone
  said zero. Blocked work comes from `bd blocked`.
- `bd list` omits gate, infra and template beads unless `--include-gates --include-infra
  --include-templates` are all passed. Measured on the same board: `bd stats` reported 45
  closed while a plain `bd list` returned 39. Every percentage built on the short list is
  quietly wrong.
- **Never write temp files to `/tmp`.** Git Bash maps `/tmp` onto `%TEMP%` while Python on
  Windows reads `/tmp` as `C:\tmp`, so the write succeeds and the next line raises
  `FileNotFoundError`. Write into `.beads/`, or read `bd` through `subprocess`.
- **Never parse `.beads/issues.jsonl`.** It is a passive export, not the board: it cannot show
  deletions, and `bd preflight` flags it as pollution. Reports read `bd … --json`.

## Git

The default profile is **conservative**: a skill reports the files it changed and the suggested
commands, and never runs `git push` or `bd dolt push` itself. As long as history stays linear
and unpushed, `git reset --hard <the first sha>` undoes an entire unattended night — that is
the only safety net these skills have, and one push destroys it.

Issues live in a local Dolt database; sync travels over `refs/dolt/data` on the git remote.
See `AGENTS.md`, "Agent Context Profiles", for the project's own policy, which wins.
